preamble: The unrounding of the short close back vowel of Middle English (/u/, lax [ʊ]; the atlas has no separate [ʊ] symbol) to the open-mid back unrounded vowel [ʌ] is the FOOT–STRUT split of Early Modern English, first clearly described in 1644. Unrounding was blocked mainly after labial consonants, leaving put, pull, full with [ʊ] beside putt, cut, dull with [ʌ]. Northern English and some Midland accents did not undergo the change.

examples.note: Unrounded and lowered in the STRUT lexical set.
Same change in the STRUT set.
Words with a preceding labial (put, pull, full) kept the rounded vowel, splitting the phoneme into FOOT /ʊ/ and STRUT /ʌ/.

sources: Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511611759
